title: Nehemiah 13: Cleansing the People, the Sabbath, and the Strange Wives
body:
Read the chapter → [Nehemiah 13](/bible/nehemiah/13)

**[Nehemiah 13:1-3](/bible/nehemiah/13#v1)**

> <sup>[1](/bible/nehemiah/13#v1)</sup> On that day they read in the book of Moses in the audience of the people; and therein was found written, that the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God for ever;
>
> <sup>[2](/bible/nehemiah/13#v2)</sup> Because they met not the children of Israel with bread and with water, but hired Balaam against them, that he should curse them: howbeit our God turned the curse into a blessing.
>
> <sup>[3](/bible/nehemiah/13#v3)</sup> Now it came to pass, when they had heard the law, that they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude.

- On that day they read in the books of Moses and found written that the Ammonite and the Moabite should not come into the congregation of God for ever, because they met not Israel with bread and water but hired Balaam against them to curse them, and the Most High turned the curse into a blessing.
- When the people heard the law, they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude. The reading of the law produced immediate obedience, cutting off what the law said to cut off.

  - **[Numbers 22:5-6](/bible/numbers/22#v5)**
    > <sup>[5](/bible/numbers/22#v5)</sup> He sent messengers therefore unto Balaam the son of Beor to Pethor, which is by the river of the land of the children of his people, to call him, saying, Behold, there is a people come out from Egypt: behold, they cover the face of the earth, and they abide over against me:
    >
    > <sup>[6](/bible/numbers/22#v6)</sup> Come now therefore, I pray thee, curse me this people; for they are too mighty for me: peradventure I shall prevail, that we may smite them, and that I may drive them out of the land: for I wot that he whom thou blessest is blessed, and he whom thou cursest is cursed.

    Balak hired Balaam to curse Israel, the history behind why the Ammonite and Moabite were shut out of the congregation.
  - **[Deuteronomy 23:3-4](/bible/deuteronomy/23#v3)**
    > <sup>[3](/bible/deuteronomy/23#v3)</sup> An Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter into the congregation of the Lord; even to their tenth generation shall they not enter into the congregation of the Lord for ever:
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/deuteronomy/23#v4)</sup> Because they met you not with bread and with water in the way, when ye came forth out of Egypt; and because they hired against thee Balaam the son of Beor of Pethor of Mesopotamia, to curse thee.

    The law itself: an Ammonite or Moabite shall not enter the congregation of the Lord for ever, because they met not Israel with bread and water and hired Balaam against them.

**[Nehemiah 13:4-9](/bible/nehemiah/13#v4)**

> <sup>[4](/bible/nehemiah/13#v4)</sup> And before this, Eliashib the priest, having the oversight of the chamber of the house of our God, was allied unto Tobiah:
>
> <sup>[5](/bible/nehemiah/13#v5)</sup> And he had prepared for him a great chamber, where aforetime they laid the meat offerings, the frankincense, and the vessels, and the tithes of the corn, the new wine, and the oil, which was commanded to be given to the Levites, and the singers, and the porters; and the offerings of the priests.
>
> <sup>[6](/bible/nehemiah/13#v6)</sup> But in all this time was not I at Jerusalem: for in the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon came I unto the king, and after certain days obtained I leave of the king:
>
> <sup>[7](/bible/nehemiah/13#v7)</sup> And I came to Jerusalem, and understood of the evil that Eliashib did for Tobiah, in preparing him a chamber in the courts of the house of God.
>
> <sup>[8](/bible/nehemiah/13#v8)</sup> And it grieved me sore: therefore I cast forth all the household stuff of Tobiah out of the chamber.
>
> <sup>[9](/bible/nehemiah/13#v9)</sup> Then I commanded, and they cleansed the chambers: and thither brought I again the vessels of the house of God, with the meat offering and the frankincense.

- Eliashib the priest, having oversight of the chambers of the house of God, was allied to Tobiah and had prepared him a great chamber where the offerings, tithes, and vessels had formerly been laid.
- Nehemiah was away in the two and thirtieth year of Artaxerxes king of Babylon, and when he returned and understood the evil, he cast all Tobiah's household stuff out of the chamber, cleansed the chambers, and brought back the vessels of the house of God with the meat offering and the frankincense.

**[Nehemiah 13:10-14](/bible/nehemiah/13#v10)**

> <sup>[10](/bible/nehemiah/13#v10)</sup> And I perceived that the portions of the Levites had not been given them: for the Levites and the singers, that did the work, were fled every one to his field.
>
> <sup>[11](/bible/nehemiah/13#v11)</sup> Then contended I with the rulers, and said, Why is the house of God forsaken? And I gathered them together, and set them in their place.
>
> <sup>[12](/bible/nehemiah/13#v12)</sup> Then brought all Judah the tithe of the corn and the new wine and the oil unto the treasuries.
>
> <sup>[13](/bible/nehemiah/13#v13)</sup> And I made treasurers over the treasuries, Shelemiah the priest, and Zadok the scribe, and of the Levites, Pedaiah: and next to them was Hanan the son of Zaccur, the son of Mattaniah: for they were counted faithful, and their office was to distribute unto their brethren.
>
> <sup>[14](/bible/nehemiah/13#v14)</sup> Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and wipe not out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God, and for the offices thereof.

- Nehemiah found that the portions of the Levites had not been given, so the Levites and singers had fled every one to his field, and he contended with the rulers and set the Levites back in their place.
- He made treasurers over the treasuries, faithful men, to distribute unto their brethren, and prayed, Remember me, O my God, concerning this, and wipe not out my good deeds that I have done for the house of my God.

**[Nehemiah 13:15-18](/bible/nehemiah/13#v15)**

> <sup>[15](/bible/nehemiah/13#v15)</sup> In those days saw I in Judah some treading wine presses on the sabbath, and bringing in sheaves, and lading asses; as also wine, grapes, and figs, and all manner of burdens, which they brought into Jerusalem on the sabbath day: and I testified against them in the day wherein they sold victuals.
>
> <sup>[16](/bible/nehemiah/13#v16)</sup> There dwelt men of Tyre also therein, which brought fish, and all manner of ware, and sold on the sabbath unto the children of Judah, and in Jerusalem.
>
> <sup>[17](/bible/nehemiah/13#v17)</sup> Then I contended with the nobles of Judah, and said unto them, What evil thing is this that ye do, and profane the sabbath day?
>
> <sup>[18](/bible/nehemiah/13#v18)</sup> Did not your fathers thus, and did not our God bring all this evil upon us, and upon this city? yet ye bring more wrath upon Israel by profaning the sabbath.

- Nehemiah saw men in Judah treading wine presses on the Sabbath, bringing in sheaves, lading asses, and bringing wine, grapes, and figs into Jerusalem on the Sabbath day, and men of Tyre selling fish and all manner of ware on the Sabbath.
- He contended with the nobles of Judah and asked what evil thing this was to profane the Sabbath day, reminding them that their fathers did the same and the Most High brought this evil upon the city, and now they brought more wrath upon Israel. Buying and selling on the Sabbath is breaking the commandment.

  - **[Exodus 20:8-10](/bible/exodus/20#v8)**
    > <sup>[8](/bible/exodus/20#v8)</sup> Remember the sabbath day, to keep it holy.
    >
    > <sup>[9](/bible/exodus/20#v9)</sup> Six days shalt thou labour, and do all thy work:
    >
    > <sup>[10](/bible/exodus/20#v10)</sup> But the seventh day is the sabbath of the Lord thy God: in it thou shalt not do any work, thou, nor thy son, nor thy daughter, thy manservant, nor thy maidservant, nor thy cattle, nor thy stranger that is within thy gates:

    The commandment to remember the Sabbath day to keep it holy and do no work, which the Sabbath commerce directly transgressed.
  - **[Jeremiah 17:21-22](/bible/jeremiah/17#v21)**
    > <sup>[21](/bible/jeremiah/17#v21)</sup> Thus saith the Lord; Take heed to yourselves, and bear no burden on the sabbath day, nor bring it in by the gates of Jerusalem;
    >
    > <sup>[22](/bible/jeremiah/17#v22)</sup> Neither carry forth a burden out of your houses on the sabbath day, neither do ye any work, but hallow ye the sabbath day, as I commanded your fathers.

    The Most High commanded to bear no burden on the Sabbath day nor bring it in by the gates of Jerusalem, the very burdens Nehemiah shut the gates against.

**[Nehemiah 13:19-22](/bible/nehemiah/13#v19)**

> <sup>[19](/bible/nehemiah/13#v19)</sup> And it came to pass, that when the gates of Jerusalem began to be dark before the sabbath, I commanded that the gates should be shut, and charged that they should not be opened till after the sabbath: and some of my servants set I at the gates, that there should no burden be brought in on the sabbath day.
>
> <sup>[20](/bible/nehemiah/13#v20)</sup> So the merchants and sellers of all kind of ware lodged without Jerusalem once or twice.
>
> <sup>[21](/bible/nehemiah/13#v21)</sup> Then I testified against them, and said unto them, Why lodge ye about the wall? if ye do so again, I will lay hands on you. From that time forth came they no more on the sabbath.
>
> <sup>[22](/bible/nehemiah/13#v22)</sup> And I commanded the Levites that they should cleanse themselves, and that they should come and keep the gates, to sanctify the sabbath day. Remember me, O my God, concerning this also, and spare me according to the greatness of thy mercy.

- When the gates of Jerusalem began to be dark before the Sabbath, Nehemiah commanded them shut and set his servants at the gates so no burden would be brought in on the Sabbath, and the merchants lodged outside Jerusalem once or twice.
- He testified against them and warned that if they came again he would lay hands on them, and from that time they came no more on the Sabbath. This laying on of hands is not a blessing but a serious warning, and the merchants knew he was not joking. He then commanded the Levites to cleanse themselves and keep the gates to sanctify the Sabbath day.

**[Nehemiah 13:23-27](/bible/nehemiah/13#v23)**

> <sup>[23](/bible/nehemiah/13#v23)</sup> In those days also saw I Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, of Ammon, and of Moab:
>
> <sup>[24](/bible/nehemiah/13#v24)</sup> And their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod, and could not speak in the Jews’ language, but according to the language of each people.
>
> <sup>[25](/bible/nehemiah/13#v25)</sup> And I contended with them, and cursed them, and smote certain of them, and plucked off their hair, and made them swear by God, saying, Ye shall not give your daughters unto their sons, nor take their daughters unto your sons, or for yourselves.
>
> <sup>[26](/bible/nehemiah/13#v26)</sup> Did not Solomon king of Israel sin by these things? yet among many nations was there no king like him, who was beloved of his God, and God made him king over all Israel: nevertheless even him did outlandish women cause to sin.
>
> <sup>[27](/bible/nehemiah/13#v27)</sup> Shall we then hearken unto you to do all this great evil, to transgress against our God in marrying strange wives?

- Nehemiah saw Jews that had married wives of Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab, and their children spake half in the speech of Ashdod and could not speak the Jews' language, but according to the language of each people.
- Because the fathers were not truly in the house, the children learned their mother's tongue and customs instead of Hebrew and the law. Nehemiah contended with them, cursed them, smote certain of them, plucked off their hair, and made them swear not to give or take daughters in marriage with those nations, reminding them that Solomon himself, though beloved of his God, was caused to sin by outlandish women.

  - **[Deuteronomy 7:3-4](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v3)**
    > <sup>[3](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v3)</sup> Neither shalt thou make marriages with them; thy daughter thou shalt not give unto his son, nor his daughter shalt thou take unto thy son.
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/deuteronomy/7#v4)</sup> For they will turn away thy son from following me, that they may serve other gods: so will the anger of the Lord be kindled against you, and destroy thee suddenly.

    The law forbids marrying the nations because they will turn the son away from following the Most High to serve other gods, and kindle his anger to destroy them.
  - **[1 Kings 11:1-4](/bible/1-kings/11#v1)**
    > <sup>[1](/bible/1-kings/11#v1)</sup> But king Solomon loved many strange women, together with the daughter of Pharaoh, women of the Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Zidonians, and Hittites;
    >
    > <sup>[2](/bible/1-kings/11#v2)</sup> Of the nations concerning which the Lord said unto the children of Israel, Ye shall not go in to them, neither shall they come in unto you: for surely they will turn away your heart after their gods: Solomon clave unto these in love.
    >
    > <sup>[3](/bible/1-kings/11#v3)</sup> And he had seven hundred wives, princesses, and three hundred concubines: and his wives turned away his heart.
    >
    > <sup>[4](/bible/1-kings/11#v4)</sup> For it came to pass, when Solomon was old, that his wives turned away his heart after other gods: and his heart was not perfect with the Lord his God, as was the heart of David his father.

    Solomon loved many strange women, and when he was old his wives turned away his heart after other gods, exactly as the law warned they would.
  - **[1 Corinthians 10:12](/bible/1-corinthians/10#v12)**
    > <sup>[12](/bible/1-corinthians/10#v12)</sup> Wherefore let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall.

    Let him that thinketh he standeth take heed lest he fall; no one is above the temptation that took Solomon down.

**[Nehemiah 13:28-31](/bible/nehemiah/13#v28)**

> <sup>[28](/bible/nehemiah/13#v28)</sup> And one of the sons of Joiada, the son of Eliashib the high priest, was son in law to Sanballat the Horonite: therefore I chased him from me.
>
> <sup>[29](/bible/nehemiah/13#v29)</sup> Remember them, O my God, because they have defiled the priesthood, and the covenant of the priesthood, and of the Levites.
>
> <sup>[30](/bible/nehemiah/13#v30)</sup> Thus cleansed I them from all strangers, and appointed the wards of the priests and the Levites, every one in his business;
>
> <sup>[31](/bible/nehemiah/13#v31)</sup> And for the wood offering, at times appointed, and for the firstfruits. Remember me, O my God, for good.

- One of the sons of Joiada, son of Eliashib the high priest, was son in law to Sanballat the Horonite, so Nehemiah chased him away because he had defiled the priesthood and the covenant of the priesthood and of the Levites.
- Thus Nehemiah cleansed the people from all strangers, appointed the wards of the priests and Levites every one in his business, and provided for the wood offering and the firstfruits, closing the book with the prayer, Remember me, O my God, for good. This is the book of records, and to see it as history rather than religion is to understand who these people are.

  - **[John 6:44](/bible/john/6#v44)**
    > <sup>[44](/bible/john/6#v44)</sup> No man can come to me, except the Father which hath sent me draw him: and I will raise him up at the last day.

    No man can come to the Most High except the Father draw him, and he draws him when he hears the words of this Bible, which is why the sheep hear his voice and a stranger they will not follow.
